key_insight: ReCAP makes a physics-informed PDE solver "plastic": it reallocates representational capacity during training by splitting, pruning, and merging local Gaussian components where residuals indicate the solution is hardest to learn.
engineering_relevance: For high-dimensional solid mechanics and other heterogeneous PDEs, this means solvers can concentrate model capacity near stress concentrations, sharp gradients, or evolving space-time features instead of wasting it in easy regions.
method: Uses responsibility-weighted residuals and residual-energy geometry to decide where to enrich the representation.
Applies local enrichment via residual-directed splitting, gate-based pruning, and function-aware merging.
Introduces quiet-child refinement to add new components while minimizing abrupt functional disturbance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation on five challenging 3D/4D PDE benchmarks against 11 physics-informed solvers, with ReCAP achieving the lowest relative L2 error on every task and improving the best competing result by 10.7%–27.5%.
watch_item: The adaptive refinement machinery adds algorithmic complexity and may require careful tuning to avoid unstable or overly aggressive structural changes during training.
paper_title: Physics-Informed Neural Plasticity: PDE Solvers That Reshape Themselves
